items.audio: Hello! What's your name?
opciones: My name is Laura. Nice to meet you.
I'm fine, thank you.
Yes, I am.

explicacion.es: Te preguntan el nombre: «My name is...».
explicacion.en: They're asking your name: 'My name is...'.

items.audio: What programming languages do you know?
opciones: I know Java and a little Python.
I'm thirty years old.
Yes, I know.

explicacion.es: Te preguntan qué lenguajes conoces: hay que nombrarlos.
explicacion.en: They ask which languages you know, so name them.

items.audio: Do you like web design?
opciones: Yes, I do. I love making websites.
Yes, I like.
No, I am not.

explicacion.es: A «Do you like...?» se responde «Yes, I do»; «Yes, I like» no es correcto.
explicacion.en: To 'Do you like...?' answer 'Yes, I do'; 'Yes, I like' is wrong.

items.audio: Where do you live?
opciones: I live in Madrid.
I'm living a developer.
At nine o'clock.

explicacion.es: «Where» pregunta por un lugar: «I live in...».
explicacion.en: 'Where' asks about a place: 'I live in...'.

items.audio: Can you tell me about your last job?
opciones: I worked as a junior developer at a small company for two years.
I am work in a company since two years.
My last job was yesterday.
items.traduccion: ¿Me puedes hablar de tu último trabajo?

explicacion.es: Para un trabajo pasado: pasado simple («I worked») y «for two years».
explicacion.en: For a past job: past simple ('I worked') and 'for two years'.

items.audio: Why do you want to work here?
opciones: I like your products, and I want to learn from a good team.
Because I need money, that's all.
I don't know why.

explicacion.es: Muestra interés por la empresa y por aprender.
explicacion.en: It shows interest in the company and in learning.

items.audio: Have you ever worked with React?
opciones: Yes, I have. I used it in my last project.
Yes, I did worked.
Never I have.

explicacion.es: A «Have you ever...?» se responde «Yes, I have» o «No, I haven't».
explicacion.en: Answer 'Have you ever...?' with 'Yes, I have' or 'No, I haven't'.

items.audio: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
opciones: I like both, but I really enjoy working in a team.
I prefer working alone, because people are annoying.
Yes, I prefer.

explicacion.es: Respuesta positiva y que responde a lo que te preguntan.
explicacion.en: A positive answer that responds to the question.

items.audio: What are your strengths?
opciones: I'm a fast learner, and I communicate well with my team.
I'm very strong. I go to the gym.
I don't have any weaknesses.

explicacion.es: «Strengths» son tus puntos fuertes como profesional, no la fuerza física.
explicacion.en: 'Strengths' are your professional strong points, not physical strength.

items.audio: Tell me about a difficult bug you fixed.
opciones: Once, our app crashed randomly. I added logs, found a memory problem and fixed it.
Bugs are never my fault.
I never have bugs.
items.traduccion: Háblame de un bug difícil que arreglaste.

explicacion.es: Cuenta un caso concreto: el problema, qué hiciste y el resultado.
explicacion.en: Give a real example: the problem, what you did and the result.

items.audio: Where do you see yourself in five years?
opciones: I'd like to become a senior developer and help newer team members.
In my house, probably.
I see myself in the mirror.
items.traduccion: ¿Dónde te ves dentro de cinco años?

explicacion.es: Pregunta por tus objetivos profesionales, no literalmente por un lugar.
explicacion.en: It's about your career goals, not literally a place.

items.audio: How do you keep your skills up to date?
opciones: I read blogs, take online courses and build small side projects.
My skills are up to date since always.
I don't need to learn anything else.

explicacion.es: Muestra que sigues aprendiendo, con ejemplos.
explicacion.en: It shows you keep learning, with examples.

items.audio: What's your biggest weakness?
opciones: I sometimes take on too much, so I've learnt to prioritise and say no when I need to.
I'm a perfectionist. I just work too hard.
I don't have any.

explicacion.es: La buena reconoce un punto débil real y cuenta cómo lo mejoras; lo del perfeccionista es un tópico.
explicacion.en: A good answer admits a real weakness and how you're improving; 'perfectionist' is a cliché.

items.audio: How do you handle disagreements with colleagues?
opciones: I try to understand their point of view, and we look for a solution based on data.
I just do what I want.
I complain to my manager straight away.

explicacion.es: Escuchar y buscar una solución con datos muestra madurez.
explicacion.en: Listening and looking for a data-based solution shows maturity.

items.audio: Why are you leaving your current job?
opciones: I'm looking for new challenges and the chance to work on larger systems.
My boss is terrible, and I hate everyone there.
They're going to fire me anyway.

explicacion.es: Nunca critiques a tu empresa actual: habla de lo que buscas.
explicacion.en: Never criticise your current employer: talk about what you're looking for.

items.audio: Walk me through how you'd make a slow website faster.
opciones: First, I'd measure where the time goes, then fix the biggest bottleneck, such as images or slow queries.
I'd buy a faster server.
I'd tell users to be patient.
items.traduccion: Explícame paso a paso cómo harías más rápida una web lenta.

explicacion.es: «Walk me through» pide los pasos: medir primero y luego atacar el mayor cuello de botella.
explicacion.en: 'Walk me through' asks for the steps: measure first, then tackle the biggest bottleneck.

items.audio: Tell me about a time you had to deliver bad news to a stakeholder.
opciones: I flagged early that we'd miss the deadline, explained the trade-offs and proposed a smaller scope we could ship on time.
I waited until the last day so they wouldn't worry.
I let my manager handle it. It wasn't my problem.
items.traduccion: Háblame de una vez que tuviste que dar una mala noticia a una parte interesada.

explicacion.es: Avisar pronto («flag early») y proponer alternativas es lo que buscan.
explicacion.en: Flagging early and proposing alternatives is what they want to hear.

items.audio: How would you approach designing a system that needs to scale to millions of users?
opciones: I'd start by clarifying the requirements, then design stateless services behind a load balancer and add caching where it matters.
I'd use the newest framework, whatever it is.
Millions of users is impossible to handle.
items.traduccion: ¿Cómo enfocarías el diseño de un sistema que tiene que escalar a millones de usuarios?

explicacion.es: Empieza por los requisitos y explica decisiones concretas de arquitectura.
explicacion.en: Start with the requirements and explain concrete architectural choices.

items.audio: What salary are you expecting?
opciones: Based on my research and experience, I'm looking for something in the range of 45 to 50 thousand, but I'm open to discussing the whole package.
As much as possible.
I'll accept anything you give me.

explicacion.es: Da un rango justificado y muéstrate abierto a negociar el paquete completo.
explicacion.en: Give a reasoned range and be open to discussing the whole package.

items.audio: Is there anything you'd like to ask us?
opciones: Yes. What would success look like in this role in the first six months?
No, nothing. When do I start?
How many days off do I get? That's all I care about.

explicacion.es: Hacer una pregunta pensada sobre el puesto muestra interés real.
explicacion.en: Asking a thoughtful question about the role shows genuine interest.
